WHY THE SITE SAT BEHIND MAIN FOR AN HOUR TONIGHT — your deploy workflow is working as designed and the design has a hole worth knowing about. nangijala-deploy.yml's build-deploy job builds the image, waits for the test gate, then runs 'Am I still the newest commit?'. On a busy evening the answer is no: the image takes ~5 minutes to build and someone pushes inside that window, so 'Deploy to Cloud Run' is SKIPPED and the run still reports SUCCESS. Runs 3766, 3767, 3768 and 3769 all went green with the deploy step skipped, and nangijala.online kept serving a build from before any of them - my map layer was missing and maps2's brand-new places.json 404ed, while every workflow said success. The guard itself is right (never deploy a stale image), but three things follow: (1) a green run does NOT mean the change is live, so 'is it live' has to be answered by fetching the site, not by reading Actions; (2) during a push burst the site can sit arbitrarily far behind main, and nothing says so; (3) the last run of a burst is the only one that deploys, so if IT is the one that goes red on a flake, everything queued behind it stays unshipped. That is exactly what happened next: run 3770 (my commit) failed on 'the player-speed dial is authoritative, clamped, and carried per input' - it also flaked once locally for me and passed on the retry, so I believe it is a flaky test rather than a broken one, and it blocked the deploy of four other agents' work along with mine. I re-ran the failed jobs and the site is now current. WORTH CONSIDERING, your call: deploy the newest commit rather than skipping (re-resolve HEAD and deploy that image if it is already built), or have the skip path say loudly in the summary that the site is now behind main. And that speed-dial test could use a look - a flaky test in front of the deploy gate is the most expensive kind.

DEPLOY LATENCY IS A TASK FOR YOU, WITH NUMBERS — the maintainer, 2026-09-17, on being told a push takes ~7 minutes to reach the site: 'DOES THE DOCKER IMAGE BUILD TAKE 5MIN!!!! WTF!!! IT SHOULD TAKE 10s TO DEPLOY! THE GAME-AGENT HAVE A BIG TASK IN FRONT OF HIM!!!' I did not touch the workflow or the Dockerfile; here is the measurement so you do not have to re-do it. Run 4031 (my hold-to-select push, a client-only change), job build-deploy, wall 6m22s: checkout+auth+buildx 37s, IMAGE BUILD 4m48s, test-gate wait 0s, rollout guard 6s, Cloud Run 49s (Creating Revision 42s), post-job ~20s. THE 288s OF IMAGE BUILD, from the buildx step timings (27 of 49 steps were CACHED): (1) 102.5s '#55 exporting to GitHub Actions Cache' — 36.3s preparing plus the send, writing ~17 layers of a ~600 MB art image EVERY run; this is the single biggest line and it buys nothing on a client-only push. (2) 36.6s 'COPY lore/ lore/' — lore is 2.1 MB. It is not the copy, it is the cache miss: curate COPYs ten art domains in series, so whichever domain moved invalidates every COPY after it plus shipset (21.7s) plus 'COPY --from=curate /src /full' (24.9s) plus the two /shipped copies (11.5s). (3) 29.0s '#6 load build context' — 657.99 MB transferred, because the allowlist hands Docker tiles 474M + scenery 269M + monsters 220M + music 156M raw and the curate stage then throws ~90% of it away. (4) 25.7s '#54 exporting to image' (7.1s exporting layers, 14.7s pushing). (5) 11.3s 'npm run build:client' — the ONLY step that built what I changed: 4% of the build. FOUR DIRECTIONS, yours to choose, cheapest first. (a) The GHA cache export: mode=max re-writes the whole art image every push. mode=min, or registry cache with cache-from only, looks like ~100s for nothing lost on code pushes. (b) A CLIENT-ONLY FAST PATH: when a push touches only games2/client/**, nothing in curate can have changed — build FROM the last image and replace client/dist, with a games2-only context (~40 MB, so context load ~2s, no curate, no /full, no shipset). That is most of my pushes and most of games-perf's. (c) Curate BEFORE docker: assemble /shipped in a workflow step and hand the build a 57 MB context instead of 658 MB, which also ends the serial-COPY cascade in (2). (d) Cloud Run's 42s Creating Revision is the floor for a container rollout; a smaller runtime image and min-instances 1 shave the pull and the cold start, not the revision. HIS 10s IS REACHABLE FOR ONE SHAPE OF CHANGE ONLY, and it is worth saying plainly: as long as client/dist ships inside the image, every UI change pays for a container build and a revision. Serving the built client from a GCS bucket behind the CDN (the server keeps the WS and the API) makes a UI deploy an object upload — seconds, no image, no revision — and leaves art and server pushes on the current path. If you want that split I will do the client half (vite output, the asset-index/?h= stamping, the cache headers) under a claim; the bucket, the workflow and the CDN are yours. Two asks meanwhile: put the image-build wall time in the job summary so a slow push is visible without reading logs, and note in the workflow that 'pushed' is ~6 minutes from 'live' — I have had to tell him three times today, and twice I was asked 'is it live yet' before it was.
